source.title: Exploring Information-Theoretic Metrics Associated with Neural Collapse in Supervised Training
source.authors: Kun Song; Zhiquan Tan; Bo-Chao Zou; Jian-Sheng Chen; Hui-Min Ma; Weiran Huang

record.file_problem: Readable full paper text with minor PDF extraction and formatting artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests grokking behavior on a modular-addition task and tracks it with matrix-information measures, rather than reproducing the original study’s measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a grokking run and its training/test accuracy and MIR/HDR dynamics. Other results on neural collapse, CIFAR classification, and fine-tuning do not test the listed grokking claims.
record.test_reason: Section VI-C reruns the Nanda et al. modular-addition setup (p=113, 30% train data, AdamW with weight decay 1). It reports train and test accuracy curves showing delayed generalization, so it bears on V1. The main aim is to use grokking as a testbed for the MIR/HDR metrics, and only one run is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. For grokking specifically, the authors say MIR and HDR show distinct two-stage behaviour and so information metrics 'can describe the Grokking phenomenon', as a basis for further research. They make no claim about mechanism or prediction.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says it follows [15] and uses modular addition, but reports a single-layer ReLU transformer with the stated architecture, p = 113, 30% training data, full-batch gradient descent, and AdamW with weight decay 1.
record.method_sensitivity: No grokking condition sweep is reported; only the stated task, data fraction, and training setup are tested.

fits_no_version.finding: During the grokking run, MIR between representations and classifier weights first rises and then falls, while HDR first falls and then rises. After grokking, MIR reaches its minimum and HDR drops sharply. This is described from Fig. 9 without numbers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information-interplay metrics between representations and the classification head show two-phase dynamics across grokking.

record.problems: The grokking evidence is one reported setting; the text gives no exact timing for the delayed test-accuracy rise, no training-set-size comparison, and no uncertainty estimates for the grokking results. MIR/HDR values are presented in a figure without numeric values in the text.

untested.parts: Only one training fraction (30%), so the claim that the delay grows as the training set shrinks is untested. The size of the delay (steps) is not quantified.
No circuit identification, no Fourier analysis, no test of memorization removal, and no progress measure shown to anticipate the jump.
No non-algorithmic grokking, and initialization scale and weight norm are not varied.
No large-model pretraining or fine-tuning test of delayed generalization.
Weight decay is fixed at 1. No critical dataset size and no ungrokking.
No comparison of algorithms across runs.
Optimizer and numerical choices are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: Grokking occupies one short subsection of a paper mainly about neural collapse and matrix-entropy losses. The CIFAR, linear-mode-connectivity, CLIP fine-tuning and semi-supervised results do not bear on any version. The record's V2 limits_scope label is removed: missing circuit analysis is an untested part, not a qualifying result. The tranche is changed to T1 because the setup follows an original source (Nanda et al.). No uncertainty estimates or step counts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports one training-set fraction only; it does not test whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks or quantify the delay.
It tracks MIR and HDR but does not identify a Fourier/generalizing circuit or show that memorizing components are removed.
No grokking-like delayed generalization is tested on non-algorithmic data, nor are initialization scale or weight norm varied to switch it on or off.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested for delayed generalization.
Weight decay is used in the grokking setup, but the paper does not test an efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The paper does not compare algorithms learned across runs.
The paper does not test optimizer or numerical-artifact explanations.

rows.subject: single-layer ReLU transformer
rows.size_stated: Token encoding dimension 128; four attention heads each of dimension 32; MLP hidden-layer dimension 512.
rows.operation_detail: Trained on modular addition, c ≡ (a + b) (mod p), with p = 113.
rows.value: The model achieves 100% training accuracy early in training.
rows.note: The text explicitly describes early perfect training fit; no exact training step is stated.

rows.subject: single-layer ReLU transformer
rows.size_stated: Token encoding dimension 128; four attention heads each of dimension 32; MLP hidden-layer dimension 512.
rows.operation_detail: Trained on modular addition, c ≡ (a + b) (mod p).
rows.baseline: Random guessing; numeric chance accuracy not stated.
rows.value: Early performance is nearly equivalent to random guessing; with continued training, test accuracy ultimately reaches 100%.
rows.note: The text describes a delayed rise after early training fit, but does not give the step count or duration.

rows.subject: single-layer ReLU transformer
rows.size_stated: Token encoding dimension 128; four attention heads each of dimension 32; MLP hidden-layer dimension 512.
rows.operation_detail: Tracked MIR between data representations and the fully connected layer during grokking.
rows.measure: Matrix Mutual Information Ratio (MIR) over training
rows.value: Figure only; the text says MIR initially increases, then begins to decrease, and reaches its lowest point after the model achieves grokking.
rows.note: The paper describes two-phase MIR dynamics but does not establish a circuit-level mechanism or quantify whether the metric anticipates the accuracy jump.
rows.check: MIR measures alignment between representations and the classifier head. It is not a circuit-level progress measure, and the figure has no readable values or timing against the accuracy jump. Not a measure of what V2 names, so it moves to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: single-layer ReLU transformer
rows.size_stated: Token encoding dimension 128; four attention heads each of dimension 32; MLP hidden-layer dimension 512.
rows.operation_detail: Tracked HDR between data representations and the fully connected layer during grokking.
rows.measure: Matrix Entropy Difference Ratio (HDR) over training
rows.value: Figure only; the text says HDR initially decreases, then begins to increase, and rapidly declines from its highest point after the model achieves grokking.
rows.note: The paper describes two-phase HDR dynamics but does not establish a circuit-level mechanism or quantify whether the metric anticipates the accuracy jump.
rows.check: Same as R3. HDR is an entropy-difference ratio between representations and classifier weights, not a measure of a generalizing circuit or of memorizing components being removed. Figure only, no numbers.

relationships.condition: Single run: one-layer ReLU transformer, modular addition p=113, 30% train data, AdamW wd=1, full batch
relationships.reason: Train accuracy hits 100% early while test accuracy is near chance, and test accuracy later reaches 100% (R1, R2). Delay length is not quantified.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy reached 100% early while test accuracy remained near chance, before test accuracy later reached 100%.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
